*** A NEW CHILD'S BAPTISM: JUSTA PASTORA, CANELONES, 9 AUGUST 1800 ***
column2: Catedral Nuestra Senora de Guadalupe, Canelones, Baptism Records 1794-1810, ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS2Z-W92K-Q: *** "En el ano del Senor de mil ochocientos a nueve dias del mes de Agosto el Presbitero Don Leon Peralta mi teniente Cura de esta Parroquia y Villa de Nuestra Senora de Guadalupe de los Canelones bautizo solemnemente a una Parvula de tres dias nacida a quien puso por nombre JUSTA PA[ST]O[R]A, hija legitima de SANCHO LLERENA y de MARIA RODRIGO, Vecinos de la misma Villa, fueron los Padrinos Juan Antonio Villegas y Maria Josefa Castro." ***
column4: *** This archive knew Justa Pastora only from her MARRIAGE of 3 November 1830 and from the 1812 padron, which gives her age as 10. *** *** Her baptism gives a birth: 6 August 1800, baptised three days later. *** The padron's 10 would put her at 1802; padron ages are rough and the act wins. *** AND IT PUTS THE FAMILY AT CANELONES IN 1800 *** - between the marriage of 1791 and the Dominga Josefa baptism of 1804, both also at Canelones, which is what the padron means when it calls all six children "naturales del Canelon".

column1: *** BUT THE MOTHER IS TRANSCRIBED 'MARIA RODRIGO', AND THAT IS NOT HER NAME ***
column2: Every other record of this couple - fourteen of them - gives the wife as *** MARIA FERNANDEZ *** , and the 1811 baptism of their son Luis gives her in full as "Dona Maria Fernandez natural de Asturias", daughter of Rodrigo Fernandez and Rosa Fernandez.
column3: *** THE DISCREPANCY IS RECORDED, NOT SMOOTHED AWAY. The image has NOT been opened. ***
column4: *** Three readings are possible and this archive is not choosing between them yet. *** (1) A machine error - but RODRIGO is not a plausible garbling of FERNANDEZ, and the same page renders other names cleanly. *** (2) The clerk wrote her FATHER'S forename by mistake - her father was RODRIGO FERNANDEZ, which would make 'Maria Rodrigo' a slip of exactly the kind a tired hand makes. *** (3) A second Sancho Llerena at Canelones, which nothing else supports. *** Reading (2) is the most economical and it only became visible on 15 September, because it depends on the 1811 act naming Rodrigo Fernandez - which this archive did not have until that morning. *** *** The image at magnification would settle it. ***

column1: *** AND TWO MORE 1804 CONFIRMATION APPEARANCES, BOTH SPONSORING ENSLAVED MEN ***
column2: Canelones, Confirmation Records 1804, three separate pages beyond the one this archive already held: *** ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS2W-73LL-5 - "Joseph Jimenez ESCLAVO DE DON LUIS JIMENEZ. P[adrino]. SANCHO LLERENA" *** ; ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS2W-73KF-W and ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS2W-73LG-X, both padrino lists carrying his name in runs of entries headed "Esclabo de...".
column4: *** This archive already recorded that in 1804 he stood godfather to 'Jose, ESCLAVO DE MANUEL LOPEZ', and in 1789 to the daughter of an indigenous man from Tucuman, and called it 'twice, fifteen years apart'. *** *** It is not twice. It is at least four times, and three of them on one day in 1804. *** A different enslaved man with a different owner - Joseph Jimenez of Don Luis Jimenez - plus two further listings. *** Whatever else he was, Sancho Llerena stood repeatedly at the font for people at the very bottom of that colony's order, and the pattern is now too consistent to read as chance. ***
